subject: English
passage: The Gini coefficient, a widely used measure of income inequality within a population, ranges from a score of zero to one. Compared with that of a highly unequal society—that is, a society where wealth is controlled by very few individuals—______
prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: a society that is more equal will have a much lower Gini coefficient.
choices.B: when a society is more equal, its Gini coefficient will be much lower.
choices.C: a more equal society will have a Gini coefficient that is much lower.
choices.D: the Gini coefficient of a more equal society will be much lower.

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer. The convention being tested is subject-modifier placement. This choice makes the noun phrase "the Gini...society" the subject of the sentence and places it immediately after the modifying phrase "compared...society." In doing so, this choice clearly establishes that the Gini coefficient of a more equal society—and not another noun in the sentence—is being compared with the Gini coefficient of a highly unequal society.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect because it results in a dangling modifier. The placement of "a more equal society" immediately after the modifying phrase illogically suggests that a society is being compared with a Gini coefficient.
